lyrics:
[Intro: a cappella four-part harmony, close and soft]
Somebody tell me whose shoes I am wearing
Whose name's on the door, whose face in the mirror is staring
I'm an ordinary man, I need no applause
But I swallowed a sentence for years, and it clawed

[Ballad: solo voice and piano, bass enters]
Mama, I said it out loud
Stood in the kitchen and I said it out loud
Forty years of yes, and I told them no
Mama, the words are out and I can't make them go

[Ballad: fuller, drums enter softly]
Mama, ooh
I know it isn't what you planned
If I'm a stranger to you now
Hold on to my hand

[Verse: piano and band, voice breaking]
Goodbye to the desk and the tie
The smile I wore like a borrowed suit
I'm not sorry, I'm terrified
I don't know what I'll do

[Guitar Solo: singing, harmonised lead guitar over the ballad chords]

[Opera: staccato piano, stacked choir, high and low voices trading]
(Who is this man?) A clerk! (A clerk?) A clerk from accounts!
(Signore, signore, he's making announcements!)
Sound the trombones, the committee's upset
(Rigatoni!) Rigatoni! (Minestrone!) Not yet!
He's only a small man from a small cul-de-sac
(Leave him his lunch break and send the man back!)
Send him back? No! We will not send him back!
(Send him back!) Never! (Send him back!) Never, never, never!
The neighbours have a pitchfork with my name on
My name on, my name on!

[Hard Rock: heavy guitar riff, full band, shouted]
You had me in a drawer with a label and a date
You had me saying sorry for arriving, being late
Oh, people, not this time, people
I'm walking out, I'm walking right out of this gate

[Guitar Break: riff climbs, drums crash, then slows]

[Coda: slow, piano and soft voice, a gong at the end]
It was only a sentence
It was only the truth
I said it in the kitchen
And the ceiling stayed a roof
Morning's coming anyway
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: Five sections. Ballad at 72 BPM in B-flat major; opera at a brisk 144 with sudden key changes; hard rock at 144 in E-flat; coda back to 72. Theatrical, shifting, larger than life.

VOICE: A male tenor with an enormous range and a theatrical delivery: tender in the ballad, operatic and exact in the middle, snarling in the rock section, hushed at the end. In the intro and opera his voice is stacked dozens of times into a choir, from a rumbling bass to a piercing falsetto, trading phrases left and right.

INSTRUMENTS: Grand piano. A lead electric guitar with a thick, singing, layered tone, often harmonised with itself. Melodic bass. A big, dry drum kit with timpani. Massed vocal overdubs used as an orchestra. A heavy, crunching guitar riff for the rock section. A single gong at the close.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, voices alone. 0:28 Ballad, piano and solo voice. 1:20 Drums enter. 1:55 Verse with the full band. 2:25 Guitar solo. 2:50 Opera: the band cuts to staccato piano and the choir takes over, with sudden stops and key changes. 3:45 Hard rock section. 4:15 Guitar break climbing and then slowing. 4:30 Coda, piano and soft voice, a gong at 4:55.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1970s maximal studio rock: tape-saturated, with huge walls of overdubbed voices and guitars, dramatic panning and extreme changes of volume.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The cut from guitar solo to staccato piano and choir at 2:50.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The confession is a middle-aged man's, and the terror is ordinary: a job, a role, a kitchen. The coda's discovery is that he told the truth and the ceiling stayed up.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Confession, fear, farce, defiance, calm.
